## ✨ Highlights

The Controller keeps up with GitHub when it's slow, and shows an
update's progress as it goes.

- 🖥️ **The Controller knows the newest release at once after a restart**:
  what it read of each release is kept on its disk, and what it hasn't
  read yet is read together, not one file after the other.
- 📶 **An update's progress shown live** on the node's **Update** page,
  whichever way the node gets the release - a download asked again
  after an error included.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- Nothing to do. The Controller writes `release-cache.json` in its data
  directory: public data about the releases, read again from GitHub if
  it's removed.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **The releases' files kept across a restart, read at once**
  ([#610](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/610), closes
  [#553](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/553)): the
  `security.json` of each release (the 🔒 badges), its checksum and its
  Controller image are kept in `release-cache.json` and read back at
  start - a Controller starting while GitHub is slow knows the newest
  release after one call, where it read some 60 files one after the
  other, minutes when GitHub answered in 8-10 s. Those not read yet are
  read eight at a time.
- **"Prepare the pre-release" has 40 seconds**: the first one after a
  publication could come back "unavailable" when the image factory
  answered after the 10 seconds every short call has.
- **The Update page shows the node's messages as they come**
  ([#611](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/611)) when the node
  downloads the release or takes uploaded files, as it already did when
  the Controller pushes it: "The node: verifying 10% - GET …: unexpected
  status 504 Gateway Timeout - trying again in 5s (2/5)" instead of
  nothing for up to two minutes per file.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- **Fewer reruns** ([#612](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/612),
  [#500](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/500)): the
  Elasticsearch log-forwarding test runs its throwaway cluster without
  disk watermarks (a runner's full disk left its security index
  unallocated), and the CI builds golangci-lint from the Go module proxy
  instead of downloading it from GitHub's release assets.
- The v2026.11.09-2 pre-release's lab campaign
  ([#609](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/609)): the CPUfreq
  warning gone from every kind of machine, the retried downloads on a
  server answering 504.
